To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep convolutional generational adversarial networks are a strong candidate to learn representations for unsupervised image generation and image classification.

(1) we introduce DCGANs, (2) we train them on various datasets, (3) we show that they learn representations of increasing levels of abstraction, and (4) we show that these learned representations are applicable for novel tasks such as image in-painting, image-to-image translation, and generating correspondences between images.
deep convolutional adverserial nets are capable of learning a hierarchy of image representations, and that these representations are suitable for a variety of image analysis tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep generative adversarial nets are a very powerful framework that is flexible and simple enough to be applied to many different problems.

we have developed a class of CNN that is well-suited for unsupervised representation learning, and have shown that it is possible to achieve unsupervised feature learning in complex datasets such as ImageNet with these networks.
we have shown a convincing evidence that deep convolutional adverserial networks can learn a hierarchy of image representations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep convolutional adversarially learned networks provide a powerful and flexible framework for unsupervised representation learning from uncurated visual data.

the deep convolutional adversarially learned representation can be used directly as an unsupervised feature extractor, and is competitive with supervised deep learning approaches on image classification, and is more effective on learning representations for image generation and invariance to image rotations.
deep convolutional adversarially learned networks are powerful, flexible, and have the capacity to learn rich hierarchical feature representations from unstructured image collections.
